bifrost: springboard/sdk/src/view/app.rs, springboard/sdk/src/document.rs, springboard/sdk/src/observable.rs, springboard/sdk/src/defaults.rs, springboard/sdk/src/restoration.rs, springboard/ui/src/nav.rs
summary: Apps are written in an imperative Rust App trait with retained views, not a declarative View/Scene/App protocol tree. Most App-structure and Data-and-storage topics have a feature-level counterpart (documents, sheets, toolbars, search field, observable values, defaults, state restoration); value-based navigation paths, an environment scope model and a preference-key model now exist as pure models but are not yet wired into views; SwiftData-style model persistence and app extensions in the SwiftUI sense have none.

features.apple: Adopting Liquid Glass, SwiftUI updates, Landmarks sample
features.note: Glass material exists in the renderer; no adoption guide or sample app for the SwiftUI API since there is no SwiftUI API

features.apple: App protocol, @main entry point, app lifecycle
features.note: App trait with hooks and a manifest; imperative, not a declarative App body
One window per app declared in the manifest; no multi-scene composition or scenePhase value

features.apple: Window, WindowGroup, openWindow, window styles and sizing
features.note: Manifest window = full-size, layout constants; no openWindow API for several windows of one app
NSDocument-style API with file grants; no declarative DocumentGroup or versioned-document UI

Push/pop stack, split view and sidebar models; NavigationPath holds value destinations and NavigationStack::apply_path rebuilds the stack from them. No destination modifier bound to views, no presented-destination bindings.
Sheets and alerts exist; popover and confirmation dialog not confirmed as separate APIs
widgets::toolbar with groups and overflow; no user toolbar customization
search_field control; no scopes, tokens or suggestions modifier
App Intents exist; no desktop widgets or extension points
Observable values with subscribers; no automatic view invalidation from dependency tracking
Environment model with nested scopes, nearest-value lookup and flags. Appearance and locale remain readable globals, not propagated through the retained views.
PreferenceKey-style trait; per-node contributions reduced in child order, with change reporting. No layout integration and no anchor preferences.
UserDefaults and state restoration cover AppStorage and SceneStorage; no SwiftData/Core Data object graph store

gaps: No multi-window openWindow API for one app
Environment and preference models are not wired into the retained views (no view-hierarchy propagation)
No SwiftData/Core Data style model store
No desktop widgets or app extension points
NavigationPath is not bound to a live navigation view or to state restoration
